xrefdescription.para: CUDA_CHECK macro catches errors and throws on failure
DeviceMemoryGuard allocates and frees GPU memory correctly
Nested RAII guards prevent resource leaks
GPU dispatch contract lock ordering prevents deadlocks
Concurrent GPU operations with resource constraints
GPUMemoryHandle RAII wrapper allocates and frees correctly
GPUEventHandle records and waits for events
Kernel timeout with fallback to CPU
Safe CUDA memory operations with validation

detaileddescription.para: A1-GPU-001: Verify allocation failure (simulated resource exhaustion) is caught and handled fail-closed.

Scenario:
Attempt to allocate extremely large GPU memory (simulating exhaustion)
Verify CudaError is thrown with appropriate error code
Verify fallback path is available for CPU execution
Expected outcome: CudaError exception is caught; system degrades gracefully.
A1-GPU-002: Verify kernel timeout enforcement.

Scenario:
Create KernelExecutionGuard with 100ms timeout
Simulate kernel execution delay exceeding timeout
Verify has_timed_out() returns true
Verify CPU fallback can be triggered
Expected outcome: Timeout is detected; CPU fallback is available.
A1-GPU-003: Verify no timeout when timeout_ms=0.

Scenario:
Create KernelExecutionGuard with timeout_ms=0 (no timeout)
Wait for extended time
Verify has_timed_out() always returns false
Expected outcome: Unbounded execution is allowed when timeout is disabled.
A1-GPU-004: Verify RAII resource cleanup on exception.

Scenario:
Attempt to allocate device memory in a try-catch block
Verify that even if allocation succeeds, destructor is called on scope exit
In a real test with hardware, verify no memory leaks occur
Expected outcome: Resources are cleaned up automatically.
A1-GPU-005: Verify all GPU failures trigger CPU fallback path.

Scenario:
Simulate various GPU errors (allocation, timeout, launch failure)
For each error, verify that CPU fallback is initiated
Verify no silent failures occur
Expected outcome: All GPU errors are caught and CPU fallback executes.
A1-GPU-006: Verify concurrent error handling (thread safety).

Scenario:
Spawn multiple threads attempting to trigger errors simultaneously
Verify each thread's error is handled independently
Verify no deadlocks or race conditions occur
Expected outcome: Each thread's error is caught; no cross-contamination.
A1-GPU-007: Verify fail-closed error classification.

Scenario:
Test various error codes from GPUDispatchErrorCode enum
Verify each non-SUCCESS code is classified as fail-closed
Verify SUCCESS is NOT fail-closed
Expected outcome: All errors trigger fail-closed behavior.
A1-GPU-008: Verify error message conversion.

Scenario:
Create CudaError with specific CUDA error codes
Verify error message includes descriptive text
Verify no nullptr or empty strings are returned
Expected outcome: All errors have descriptive messages.
A1-GPU-009: Verify timing utilities work correctly.

Scenario:
Test ms_to_us conversion
Test us_to_ms conversion
Verify round-trip conversion preserves values
Expected outcome: Conversions are accurate.
A1-GPU-010: Verify stream guard compiles and has correct semantics.

Scenario:
Verify CudaStreamGuard can be move-constructed
Verify copy operations are deleted
Verify move semantics work correctly
Expected outcome: Correct RAII and move semantics.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1: All 8 use-after-free findings resolved
Test: Verify that move-only semantics prevent use-after-free
ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2: All GPU allocations protected by RAII
Test: Verify make_unique_gpu covers all allocation paths
ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3: Zero uninitialized access
Test: Verify all allocations are zero-initialized or checked
ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 4: C++17 best practices (smart pointers, RAII, move semantics)
Test: Verify codebase uses modern C++ idioms
